item.title: Send sensor data to Telegram using an ESP32
item.description: Clovis Fritzen shows how to send sensor data to Telegram, using an ESP32 microcontroller Arduino code to create a weather station. item.title: Zork I, II, and III go Open Source
item.description: Microsoft states they are preserving a cornerstone of gaming history that is near and dear to their hearts. Microsoft’s Open Source Programs Office (OSPO), Team Xbox, and Activision are making Zork I, Zork II, and Zork III available under the MIT License. item.title: The Quantum Quest for a Perfectly Random d20 #DnD #Gamer #RNG
item.description: Most random number generators aren’t actually random. Standard computers are only capable of generating Pseudo-random numbers: numbers that appear random but are in fact predictable. To get truly random you might need to get quantum. item.title: From the Adafruit Learning System: Hacking Holiday Animatronics
item.description: The typical holiday animatronic will contain inputs, such as buttons and light/motion sensors, and outputs, such as motors, lights, and speakers. Learning to identify the parts of your animatronic will aid you in transplanting your own control system. Check out the guide from John Park and make your own this holiday season!

item.title: Pico-100BASE-TX: RP2040/RP2350 bit-banged 100 MBit/s Ethernet @raspberry_pi
item.description: The Pico-100BASE-TX library allows a microcontroller to stream out data with around 11 MByte/s from a RP2040 or RP2350 MCU using the PIO to bit-bang a 100 MBit/s Fast Ethernet connection.
